findings.claim: ImageQueryDropTarget keeps the drag class 'upload' after an upload-class drag leaves the page without dropping, because onDragLeave returns early unless the class is one_image and only onDrop or unmount reset it.
findings.impact: On the text-query page with image search available, drag a PDF or several files over the page, move out, then drag a single image in. dragClass is still 'upload', so it is not reclassified: no overlay shows and the image drop does nothing. The class is no longer taken at the dragenter of each drag, as I8 requires. Only a later drop or a remount clears it.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/search/ImageQueryDropTarget.tsx:50-53 classifies only when dragClass === null; :65-69 onDragLeave returns when dragClass !== 'one_image', so reset() is not called for the upload class; reset runs only in onDrop (:78) and the effect cleanup (:93). ImageQueryDropTarget.test.tsx 'classes again after the drag leaves' covers only a one-image drag leaving, not an upload-class one.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read only). Steps: dragenter with a text file on the frame, dragleave, dragenter with one PNG, then drop. Expected: overlay and onImageQuery. Actual by reading: no overlay, no call. Mutation: none needed; add a test with an upload-class dragenter then dragleave then a one-image dragenter and drop; it would fail.

bucket_proposal.reason: I8 says the action of a drop is the class given to that drag at its dragenter; a stale class from an earlier abandoned drag changes the outcome of a later one-image drag.

findings.proposed_fix: Count depth for every file drag regardless of class and call reset() when depth reaches 0 in dragleave, or also reset on dragend and on a dragenter after the counter reached zero.

findings.claim: The real-browser drop-target spec dispatches synthetic DragEvents on the frame element and its hit-test assertion `el?.closest(...) !== null` is also true when elementFromPoint returns null.
findings.impact: The spec proves the overlay does not block hit testing in the normal case, but it cannot catch a real dragleave/dragenter sequence on the frame, and a null hit would pass. Weak guard for the r7 overlay finding.
findings.evidence: frontend/e2e-components/image-drop-target-desktop.spec.ts: page.evaluate uses `el?.closest("[data-page-frame]") !== null`; undefined !== null is true. Events are dispatched with dispatchEvent, not by CDP drag as image-search-drag-desktop.spec.ts does.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariant is broken by the code; the test is weaker than it reads.

findings.proposed_fix: Assert `el !== null && el.closest(...) !== null`, and drive the drag with Input.dispatchDragEvent.

specification_compliance: r7 F1 (overlay intercepting the drop) is addressed: the overlay has pointer-events-none and a real-browser fixture checks elementFromPoint falls through to the frame.
r7 F2 (no test for absent onImageQuery) is addressed by two unavailable-state tests, although the two new tests are nearly identical.
r7 F3 (listener churn) is addressed: the callback is held in a ref and the effect depends on the boolean enabled.
I8 is only partly met: a one-image drop starts a query and never uploads, but the drag class can go stale after an abandoned upload-class drag (F1).
I7: with no onImageQuery no listener is attached and no preventDefault is called, which matches the tests.
regression_risks: The effect looks up [data-page-frame] once at mount. If the frame element is replaced later (a loading state rendering a different PageFrame), the listeners stay on the detached element.
hasFiles now accepts any item of kind file, which widens what counts as a file drag on the page.
test_coverage: ImageQueryDropTarget.test.tsx now covers unavailable state, pointer-events-none on the overlay, class kept through nested dragenters, no fallback to upload and reclass after a one-image drag leaves.
No test covers an upload-class drag that leaves without dropping followed by a one-image drag (F1).
The new real-browser spec uses synthetic events and a weak null check (F2).

trajectory: The round removes more than it adds. It holds the callback in a ref and keys the effect on a boolean, which removes listener churn and mid-drag resets. It adds pointer-events-none, which is a class and not a state. It adds one branch to hasFiles (the items check). It adds tests, with no new flag or state. The defect left is the same shape as before: a drag class held in a closure variable that only some paths reset, which is the drag logic that moved out of UploadZone. I see convergence, not further patching, but the reset logic still needs a single path.
